messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty — HIGH: ELB 5xx spike detected in us-west-2a (azc). Affected service: inference-api-prod. Pager: Sam H. — https://redwood.incidents/2248001234
Sam H.: oncall here. seeing alerts: 5xx up to 18% and p95 latency spike for a subset of customers in US-WEST-2, started ~22:04 UTC
Priya K.: same. Dashboards show ELB 502/504 surge, several targets reporting connection resets. Any NATGW or ENI errors?
Jia L.: pulling forward logs now. ELB access logs show backend_status=502 backend_connection_errors=1 and lots of "connection reset by peer" entries. EC2 instance ENI counters show TX drops in azc.
Marta R.: running a NATGW health check. `aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --region us-west-2 --filter Name=status,Values=available` -> NATs present but CloudWatch shows >50% packet drops on natgw-0a1b2c3d for the subnet in us-west-2a.
Alex P.: Route53 health checks for inference-api-prod (hc-9a8b7c) are failing only from probes in us-west-2a. Other AZ probes are green.
Sam H.: early hypothesis: partial AZ egress path degradation (NATGW/ENI) causing connection resets on backend requests that need external egress (third-party token calls, telemetry). Static model inference (no external calls) seems fine. Impact approx ~15% of overall traffic in us-west-2.
Priya K.: mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic off the affected AZ by adjusting ELB target weights & enable cross-zone, 2) replace failing NATGW, 3) update Route53 weighted records/health failover to favor healthy AZs, 4) scale up backends in healthy AZs.
Jia L.: deregistering unhealthy targets from tg-0f1e2d3c now: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/tg-0f1e2d3c --targets Id=i-0abcde12345` — doing one AZ batch at a time.
Sam H.: enabling ELB cross-zone balancing to reduce impact for clients pinned to an AZ: `aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --attributes Key=load_balancing.cross_zone.enabled,Value=true`
IncidentBot: Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/az-egress-deg — checklist updated with NATGW failover steps.
Marta R.: spun up replacement NATGW in affected subnet (natgw-0f9e8d7c) and updated route table rtb-zzz to point to the new ENI. Propagation underway (~30s-2m).
Alex P.: kicking a Route53 weight change to shift 70% traffic to us-west-2b/c using a weighted policy: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://shift-weights.json`
Priya K.: support note: we're seeing customer-facing 502s on streaming endpoints (long polls). Notifying Support to prepare status page & customer comms.
Sam H.: after NAT replacement + ELB cross-zone + target cleanup, error rate dropped from ~18% to ~4% within ~8 minutes. Some residual 5xx for clients still pinned to the problematic AZ.
PagerDuty: Reminder: if incident exceeds 30m, do a full handoff and create incident postmortem in #postmortems.
Jia L.: increasing ASG capacity in healthy AZs to absorb shifted load: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name inference-prod-asg --min-size 6 --desired-capacity 8` — instances launching now.
Sam H.: handing off to Priya for next 2 hours. Priya, you'll own mitigation, monitoring, and customer comms.
Priya K.: taking ownership. Drafting status update: "We are investigating a partial network egress degradation in us-west-2 impacting some customers. Mitigation is in progress — traffic is being shifted to healthy AZs and we are replacing an impacted NAT gateway. Some latency/errors may persist. Next update in 30 minutes." Sam, approve?
Sam H.: approved. Add note: customers on Dedicated pools may see transient failures; advise retries.
Marta R.: NAT route propagation complete for the replacement, packet drops back to baseline on new NATGW, old natgw-0a1b2c3d flagged for AWS investigation.
Alex P.: opening AWS support case (case id TBD) for possible carrier/equipment issue in us-west-2a — attaching ELB logs, NATGW metrics, and traceroutes.
Sam H.: Logged incident INC-2248001234. Handoff: Priya K. (owner). Remaining tasks: monitor for 2h, validate customer retry behavior, publish status page message, and create postmortem doc.
Priya K.: coordinating with SRE + Support for customer callbacks and SLA checks. Scheduling incident review tomorrow at 14:00 PST.
IncidentBot: INC-2248001234 — status updated: mitigation in progress → partial recovery observed. Participants: Sam H., Priya K., Jia L., Marta R., Alex P.
Sam H.: thanks team. If error rate spikes again, ping @pager and call me directly.
Priya K.: acknowledging handoff and taking over monitoring. :wave:
